g: Used before different, before comparatives with more and less, and idiomatically before other comparatives.
It is a less physical kind of torture, but no less gruesome.
(informal) Used idiomatically before certain other adjectives.
I just want to find out whether she's coming or no.
(colloquial, usually humorous) Not, does not, do not, etc.
We'll be finished in no time at all.
Not any possibility or allowance of (something).
Not (a); not properly, not really; not fully.
A negating expression; an answer that shows disagreement, denial, refusal, or disapproval.
A vote not in favor, or opposing a proposition.

Used to show disagreement, negation, denial, refusal, or prohibition.

Used to express sadness or disappointment.
I got the job! / No! Really? That's fantastic!
Used to show agreement with a negative question.

(transitive, colloquial) To answer with “no”; to decline, reject.
(idiomatic) Designating drinks that contain little or no alcohol.

(cricket, of a bowler) To bowl a no ball.
(cricket, of an umpire) To call and signal a no ball.

(Internet slang) Used at the beginning of a sentence to add emphasis or to express astonishment.
Used to indicate that something is trivial or unimportant.

Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see no, big whoop.
(US) Used to minimize the importance of something
Give a call, we'll talk, no big whoop.
(idiomatic, colloquial) Synonym of no big deal: not important, not something to worry about.

(slang, often ironic) Synonym of no big deal.

(US, informal, mildly humorous) Not good; no good; bad.

One who does not change, or opposes a change.
